text:
maria: Hey team, fyi I ran a targeted perf sweep after last week's kernel-selector change. Seeing a 12-18% drop in tokens/sec for long-sequence KV-heavy workloads on A100/H100 only. Logs + perf CSV attached in GDrive link: https://go/reports/kv-kernel-sweep-2790123456 :eyes:
aj: Thanks — looked at the CSV. p50 roughly same, but p95/p99 spike on >5120 token requests. The selector is preferring the new fused-attn path which fragments KV pages and prevents large continuous packing.
maria: Exactly. The fused path reduces per-token compute for short seqs but causes KV cache fragmentation for long contexts + packing. We see memory churn and more CUDA memcpys.
zack: Any quick mitigations? Could we force kernel-selector fallback for requests with kv_present && seq_len > 4096?
ryan: We can, but it needs a safe heuristic. Suggest introducing a per-GPU max_tokens_per_batch override that the scheduler enforces before kernel selection. Example target caps I prototyped: {"A100": "128000", "H100": "160000", "A10": "64000", "L4": "48000", "T4": "32000"} — these are token-budget-per-batch not per-request.
maria: Those numbers look reasonable. On A100/H100 the issue mostly hits when large requests pack with many small ones; token budgets get split into many fragments. Capping the batch token budget seems sane.
azj: (typo) aj: I ran a short canary with A100 cap 128k, selector allowed fused-attn only for batches <64k and fallback otherwise. p99 dropped back to baseline in 20m run. Graph: https://go/graphs/2790123456-canary
zack: We should codify queue policy too: prefer time-window aggregation for KV-heavy class and size-window for small inference. Propose queue policy flags: `kv_aware_time_window_ms` and `kv_fragmentation_threshold` (float). Example snippet: ```json
{
  "kv_aware_time_window_ms": 6,
  "kv_fragmentation_threshold": 0.75,
  "max_tokens_per_batch_overrides": {
    "A100": 128000,
    "H100": 160000,
    "A10": 64000,
    "L4": 48000,
    "T4": 32000
  }
}
```
ryan: Love it. Add a selector toggle `force_kernel_fallback_on_kv_frag` so ops can flip without deploy.
maria: Also want telemetry: emit `kv_frag_ratio` on every batch and `kernel_choice_reason` (latency_estimate/size_based/override). That helped us debug during the canary.
ci-bot: experiment scheduled: canary-run (A100 cluster) by ryan at 2026-03-18T15:10Z for 30m. Job id: exp-2790123456-canary.
sre-bot: Heads up — we'll throttle burst capacity if p99 > 1s for >10min during test. Add alert rule `canary-kv-kernel-p99` to paging-slo channel.
aj: One more note: kernel compile flags differ on L4/T4; fused-attn isn't always faster there. For L4/T4 we should default to the legacy path unless perf proves otherwise.
maria: Agreed. So plan summary: 1) add max_tokens_per_batch_overrides per-GPU (numbers above), 2) add queue flags kv_aware_time_window_ms + kv_fragmentation_threshold, 3) selector toggle for forced fallback, 4) extra telemetry, 5) canary on A100 then H100, then rollout.
zack: I'll open a PR with config + selector toggle. Will include tests to simulate high KV fragmentation workloads (unit + integration).
ryan: I'll run 2h stress job after canary on H100 cluster. Test matrix: baseline / capped / capped+timewindow. Measure tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, memcpy counts and kernel switch rate.
maria: Leaving the exact threshold numbers flexible but start with fragmentation_threshold=0.75 and time_window=6ms. If we see underpacking, lower cap by 10%.
aj: Ack. Also add a regression test that runs during kernel-selector merges to prevent accidental re-enable of fused path on large-KV batches.
ci-bot: PR created: https://go/repo/pulls/2567 by zack - includes config + tests.
maria: Thanks. We'll retrigger perf dashboards after PR merged. Tagging @ryan @aj for canary ops. :thumbsup:
ryan: On it.
zack: I'll drop the PR link in the canary run notes.
maria: Great work team. If we hit any surprises during canary, revert selector via the new toggle and escalate. :rocket:
